text.p: Paul Stankowski tapped in for a short birdie on the 18th hole of the Plantation course Sunday to win the $1.1 million Kapalua International by one stroke over two-time former champion Fred Couples.

Stankowski, who started the day with a one-shot lead, fired a five-under-par 68 and had to birdie the final hole after Couples birdied to move to 20-under. Stankowski won the $198,000 first prize with a four-round total of 21-under 269.
The 56-man field used both the Plantation and Bay courses over the first two rounds, but played the final 36 holes at the par-73 Plantation layout.
Stankowski, who became one of 13 first-time winners on the PGA Tour in April with a playoff victory at the BellSouth Classic, boosted his 1996 winnings to $588,575.

Davis Love III and U.S. Open champion Steve Jones tied for third at 19-under. Briton Sandy Lyle and former tournament champion Bob Gilder were four shots off the pace at 17-under 273. Jones and Gilder shared the lead after each of the first two rounds.
The Kapalua International is not a sanctioned PGA event and the top five players on the PGA money list skipped it, as did 20-year-old sensation Tiger Woods.
